source_message.text:
Full list:

\- J\_BTN3 — panel button, GPIO6
\- J\_BTN4 — panel button, GPIO7
\- J\_SW — panel slide switch, GPIO8
\- J\_RESET — panel reset button, EN to GND
\- J\_TOUCH — capacitive touch (TTP223), GPIO11
\- J\_TOUCH2 — capacitive touch (TTP223), GPIO14
\- BOOT button — on-board only (development use, not panel-mounted)

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: they are connected with connectors, only button on board is boot

value_updates.control_mounting: panel controls connected through board connectors

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
have some things here which might or might not be issues — you tell me if some are really issues, and if not that's OK, just explain to me:

1\. Buttons 3, 4 and the slide switch. The connectors CN17 / CN19 / CN20 short the GPIO to GND when the button is pressed, but R16 / R17 / R18 are also pull-DOWNS to GND on the same nets. So the GPIO would be LOW pressed AND LOW released. Did you mean the resistors to be pull-UPS to +3V3 instead, or to put +3V3 on connector pin 1?

ambiguity.description: The controls short their GPIOs to ground when pressed, but the design also uses pull-downs, leaving the intended released-state biasing unresolved between 3.3V pull-ups and a connector-side 3.3V arrangement.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Thanks Dusko, all clear:
1. VRTC — agreed, NC for v1 (no external RTC chip on this board). But while we're on the RTC topic — I think I confused VRTC and VBACKUP earlier. VBACKUP (pin 27) is the input for backup power to keep the AXP2101's internal RTC alive when the main battery is removed. Could you also route VBACKUP to a small test pad / via alongside PWROK from item #10? That way we can later fit a 100 µF cap (\~2-3 min hot-swap tolerance), a supercap (\~weeks), or a CR1220 coin cell (\~4 years) for real time-keeping if we ever want it. No need to populate anything now — just expose the pad.
2. Buttons (R16/R17/R18) — agreed, change those three to pull-ups to 3V3 (active LOW: connector pin 1 stays GND, press shorts GPIO to GND). I've updated <http://pcb-integrated.md|pcb-integrated.md> to match.
3. PIR (R19) and Touch (R20/R25) — these are correct as pull-downs. Both AM312 (PIR) and TTP223 (touch) have push-pull active-HIGH outputs, so the sensor's internal driver overrides the 10 k pull-down when active. Pull-down to GND just gives a defined LOW state when the sensor is unplugged. No change needed.
